**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Enforce the claimed daily boundary limit**

When a second session boundary occurs on the same day, the Stop checklist still directs the orchestrator to create and auto-merge another boundary PR, and the SKILL explicitly permits `boundary-<date>-2`; meanwhile `scripts/check-regime-boundary.sh` contains no date or boundary-merge-history check. Thus `make check-regime-boundary` can pass while the new once-a-day invariant is violated. Either implement the promised check and reconcile the multi-boundary procedure, or stop claiming that this command enforces the limit. The task's residual control for this trust-boundary rule therefore does not mitigate the behavioral mismatch.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L78-L78](https://github.com/mryfmo/dotfiles/blob/becba33c616247057f2f75cf30ec5aefcbf00592/AGENTS.md#L78-L78)

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Report both Bot reviews after the fix round**

When a P0/P1 survives the worker-side fix round, this workflow has already received the initial review and explicitly requests another `@codex review`; line 207 also defines the review count as `1 + the fix rounds`, so this scenario has two Bot rounds, not one. Emitting `bot_rounds=1` underreports the review history and makes the RESULT evidence inconsistent; use `bot_rounds=2` here and in the Message Contract, or rename the field if it is intended to count fix rounds. The threat-table control merely pins both contradictory sentences in tests, so it does not mitigate this mismatch.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L78-L78](https://github.com/mryfmo/dotfiles/blob/61dbd68e6bb72b1bc0420f3e1b93b7c064fdbce3/AGENTS.md#L78-L78)
